acceptance: Each reviewer either returned a complete findings list or is recorded as unavailable or waived by the user, with date and reason
Every returned finding has a recorded ruling (accept, partly accept, or rebut) with file:line or packet evidence; no finding is silently dropped
Every accepted finding is reflected in the description, acceptance, or needs of a named pvm-* item, and the item IDs are listed in this item's context
Reviewers ran read-only: codex with --sandbox read-only; agy in a detached worktree created at the reviewed revision and removed afterwards; git status in the main checkout is unchanged
The user's explicit approval to begin implementation (pvm-s0a onward) is recorded in context with date and wording; reviewing or creating items does not count as approval
context: 2026-10-07: codex usage limit resets 18:17 local time; agy quota reset roughly 2 hours after 15:40 local. Review packet format: role (findings only), goal, output contract (ID, severity, target, finding, evidence, recommended change; at most 15; ends "No further findings.").
description:
Decision gate before any implementation of the Polars version matrix. The plan (umbrella item pvm-polars-2-version-matrix) has had one complete external review (muse-spark-1.3) and one partial one: codex (gpt-6.1-sol) hit its usage limit after raising two leads, and agy (gemini-3.8-flash) never ran because of quota. Both leads were verified and are already in the plan (DataFrame validation cannot return a clean pass outside TPC-H SF1; Polars scalar() collects bypass the engine setting).

Work: re-run codex (gpt-6.1-sol, medium effort, read-only sandbox) and agy (gemini-3.8-flash-high, plan mode, detached worktree, evidence inline because headless agy cannot run tools) against the current item set. Rule on every finding (accept / partly accept / rebut, with file:line evidence). Apply accepted findings with update_item to the affected pvm-* items.

Decision gate: the user decides whether to wait for these reviews or to waive them. A waiver must be recorded in context with the date and the user's words.
